subject: Algebra 2 - Polynomial Functions

questions.description: Factor f(x) = 8x^4 - 8x^3 - 70x^2 + 120x completely, then list all real zeros
For each expression, state whether it is a polynomial and give its degree

parts_detail.A: Expression not identified by Kai — no explanation given
parts_detail.B: (1/3)x^2 + (2/3)x — Kai said Degree 4 (wrong, correct degree is 2)
parts_detail.D: 3^x — Kai said Degree 3 (wrong: 3^x is exponential, not a polynomial at all)

questions.kai_answer: A: no answer; B: degree 4; C: degree 0; D: degree 3
questions.correct_answer: A: polynomial, state degree; B: polynomial, degree 2; C: polynomial, degree 0; D: NOT a polynomial (variable in exponent)
questions.notes: Only C was correct. Kai missed that (1/3)x^2+(2/3)x is degree 2 (not 4), and that 3^x is exponential not polynomial.

questions.description: Write the equation of the polynomial graphed: touches x-axis at x=1, crosses at x=3 and x=6, passes through (2,36)
Find r given y = (x+r)(x-2)^2 has y-intercept (0,12)
Expand and simplify to standard form: f(x) = (x-2)^2(5x-18) + some given polynomial setup
Use the Factor Theorem: is (x+5) a factor of f(x)? Evaluate f(-5).
questions.kai_answer: f(-5) = -54, not zero, so (x+5) is NOT a factor
questions.correct_answer: f(-5) = -54 ≠ 0, so (x+5) is not a factor

questions.description: From graph of f(x): describe end behavior, state odd/even degree, positive/negative leading coefficient, state degree, list real zeros

parts_detail.a: End behavior: as x→-∞, f→+∞; as x→+∞, f→-∞

questions.kai_answer: (a) x to +inf: y to -inf, x to -inf: y to +inf (correct); (b) odd (correct); (c) positive, left down right up (WRONG, should be negative); (d) degree 5 (correct); (e) x=-4,-1,1,3 no multiplicities (WRONG, correct is x=-4 mult 2, x=-1 mult 1, x=2 mult 2)
questions.correct_answer: End behavior up-left/down-right; odd; negative LC; degree 5; zeros x=-4 (mult 2), x=-1 (mult 1), x=2 (mult 2)
questions.notes: Kai wrote end behavior arrows correctly in (a) but contradicted himself in (c) by saying positive LC. Graph goes up-left/down-right = negative LC. For (e), Kai listed x=-4,-1,1,3 with no multiplicities. Correct zeros are x=-4 (mult 2), x=-1 (mult 1), x=2 (mult 2). He had wrong zeros and missing multiplicities.

questions.description: Factor f(x) = 2x^3 - 8x^2 - 24x completely, write in factored form, find all zeros
Find all zeros of f(x) = x^3 - 9x^2 + 7x + 14 using the table of values provided
questions.correct_answer: x = 2, x = √7, x = -√7  [divide out (x-2), then x^2-7=0 gives x=±√7]
questions.notes: Kai found x=2 from the table but stopped. Must divide (x-2) out to get x^2-7=0, yielding x=±√7 (irrational real zeros that won't appear in an integer table).

questions.description: Find ALL zeros of y = x^3 + 8x^2 - 43x + 60 given the graph shows (-12,0) and (0,60)
questions.correct_answer: x = -12 (real); x = 2+i, x = 2-i (complex conjugates)  [divide by (x+12), then x^2-4x+5=0 → discriminant -4 → x=2±i]
questions.notes: Kai found x=-12 from the graph but stopped. Must divide by (x+12) to get x^2-4x+5=0. Discriminant=16-20=-4 (negative), so two complex zeros x=2±i. 'Find all zeros' includes imaginary zeros.

standards_summary.S1_polynomial_expressions: Strong — long division clean, factoring multi-step problems solid
standards_summary.S2_solving: Strong — Factor Theorem mastered, factored form reliable
standards_summary.S3_graphing: Strong — end behavior, degree, leading coefficient all correct
standards_summary.S4_polynomial_identification: Needs work — Q2 shows gaps in explaining WHY something is/isn't a polynomial
standards_summary.finding_all_zeros: Incomplete — Q11 and Q12 both show pattern of stopping after first zero instead of continuing to divide and factor

focus_areas: Q2: Polynomial identification — must explain reasoning, know 3^x is exponential not polynomial, know degree = highest exponent on variable
Q11 and Q12: Finding ALL zeros — after finding one zero from a table or graph, always divide it out and solve the remaining factor (irrational or complex zeros won't show in tables)
